title: Criminal Complaint: State of Wisconsin v. Tehrangi N. Chapman

reports.title: Second member of the Milwaukee Police Department charged with misuse of license plate reader system
Criminal Complaint: State of Wisconsin v. Tehrangi N. Chapman

summary:
Milwaukee Police Detective Tehrangi Chapman has been charged with felony misconduct in public office and misuse of a GPS device. Investigators say he used the department’s Flock license plate reader system 20 times to track two people without a law enforcement purpose. He allegedly searched one person’s plate 17 times between January 2024 and January 2025 and placed a GPS tracker on that person’s vehicle. He also searched another person’s plate three times in January 2025, claiming the reason was training. Chapman, a 22-year veteran assigned to internal affairs, had previously investigated another officer for similar misuse.

Police Chief Jeffrey Norman said everyone must follow the law, and Fire and Police Commissioner Krissie Fung called the charges troubling for public trust. Chapman has been suspended since March 13 and is scheduled to appear in court on July 17. The case follows Officer Josue Ayala, who pleaded guilty to attempted misconduct and resigned. Several Wisconsin communities have ended contracts with Flock Safety over privacy and misuse concerns.
